features.title: Guest sign-ins
features.summary: People create their own temporary Windows account in the guest portal and sign in at any shared PC as a standard user.
facts: The guest, from the guest portal, without staff
Shown once, generated with 14 characters by default

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The guest portal asks for an optional display name and how long the sign-in should last. The TempDesk Agent creates the account in the guest OU (`OU=Guests,OU=TempDesk`), adds it to the `TempDesk Guests` group, sets the expiry on the account itself (`accountExpires`) and returns the user name and password once. The guest then signs in at any TempDesk PC with `DOMAIN\guest-xxxxxx`.

sections.title: Limits that protect the domain
sections.body:
- A per-address limit (`guestCreatePerHour`, default 20) and a global cap of active guests (`guestMaxActive`, default 200).
- Guests cannot change their password and cannot reach any admin route, even with a stolen session token.
- Guests can check their own status or delete their own account with their password, if the owner allows it (`allowSelfDelete`).

sections.title: Choices offered
sections.body: Expiry choices come from the settings document (1 hour, 4 hours, 1 day, 1 week, and optionally permanent until deleted). Administrators can also create guests with any duration and extend them from the admin console.

features.title: Expiry and cleanup
features.summary: A warning, a sign-out at the end, then the account and the local profile are deleted. Nothing is left behind.
facts: Checked every 2 minutes on each PC
Account reaper every 5 minutes, profile cleanup at startup and hourly

sections.title: Three independent safety nets
sections.body:
1. **Session watcher** (`client/Watch-GuestSession.ps1`): Active Directory blocks new sign-ins after expiry but does not end open sessions, so the watcher warns the guest and then signs the session out once the account has expired, been disabled or deleted.
2. **Guest reaper** (`server/Invoke-GuestReaper.ps1` and the agent): deletes expired accounts that live in the guest OU and carry the `TempDesk guest` description. Nothing else is touched.
3. **Profile cleanup** (`client/Remove-GuestProfiles.ps1`): removes local profiles of guests whose account is gone, disabled or expired, using Win32_UserProfile so the folder and registry entries both go.

sections.title: What is never removed
sections.body: Profiles that are loaded, special or system profiles, and any account outside the guest OU. Profile names must also start with the guest prefix before they are considered.

features.title: App allowlist
features.summary: Guests run only the programs you list. Everything is enforced by Group Policy for standard users.
facts: RestrictRun list for the guest group

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The admin console edits one list of executable names (for example `msedge.exe`, `chrome.exe`, `WINWORD.EXE`). The agent writes it to the guest user GPO as the `RestrictRun` list, so Windows Explorer starts only those programs for guests. Turn the list off to allow everything a standard user can run.

sections.title: Why guests are standard users
sections.body: Nothing in TempDesk grants guests administrator rights. Installers that need elevation fail for guests; machine-wide apps are installed by startup scripts that run as SYSTEM instead.

features.title: Preset apps
features.summary: Chrome, VS Code, Git, Node.js, Python, Claude desktop and Claude Code, Codex desktop and CLI, and Desktop Material are ready on every PC.
facts: Installed at startup as SYSTEM with winget
Installed in the background at sign-in
Presetup > Startup scripts in the admin console

sections.title: Installed at startup (machine-wide)
sections.body:
`client/defaults/startup/10-Install-GoogleChrome.ps1` installs Google Chrome from the Chrome Enterprise MSI (from SYSVOL if you put it there, otherwise from Google) and refuses an MSI whose Authenticode signature is not Google's.

`client/defaults/startup/20-Install-DeveloperTools.ps1` installs with winget in machine scope: Git, Visual Studio Code, GitHub CLI, Node.js LTS, Python 3.13, PowerShell 7, .NET 8 and .NET 10 Desktop Runtimes, the Visual C++ Redistributable, 7-Zip, Notepad++, Claude Code (CLI) and the Codex CLI (npm package `@openai/codex`). Packages that are already installed are skipped, so later boots are quick.

sections.title: Installed at sign-in (per user)
sections.body: `client/defaults/logon/20-Install-UserApps.ps1` re-launches itself hidden so sign-in is not delayed, then installs Claude (desktop), Codex (desktop, from the Microsoft Store) and Desktop Material (checked against the SHA-256 digest GitHub publishes for the asset). These go into the guest's own profile and disappear with it.

sections.title: Make it yours
sections.body: Every script is visible and editable in the admin console. Add your own `.ps1` or `.cmd` files; they run in name order.

features.title: Wi-Fi profiles
features.summary: Publish Wi-Fi networks once and every TempDesk PC connects before anyone signs in.
facts: SYSVOL TempDesk\wifi, readable by Domain Computers and Domain Admins only

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The admin console writes each network as WLAN profile XML to SYSVOL. The computer startup script installs every published profile with `netsh wlan add profile` and removes profiles that were deleted. Because the folder is readable only by computers and domain admins, guests cannot read the keys.

features.title: Admin console
features.summary: Every directory object, every Group Policy setting and the server itself, managed in a browser.
facts: Every Administrative Template setting and the security settings

sections.title: Directory
sections.body: Browse the tree, search with LDAP filters, create, edit, move and delete any object, reset passwords, unlock and enable accounts and manage group membership. Binary values are shown as base64. Objects protected from accidental deletion need an explicit force.

sections.title: Group Policy
sections.body: Create and link GPOs, edit status, permissions, WMI filters and inheritance, back up and restore. **Administrative Templates** are read from the central store (ADMX and en-US ADML) and shown as real forms: enabled, disabled or not configured, with every element (text, number, list, enum, check box). **Security settings** edit GptTmpl.inf (password and lockout policy, Kerberos, user rights, audit, security options) through a built-in catalog instead of raw text.

sections.title: Server management
sections.body: Overview with live CPU, memory, disk and network charts; services, processes, event logs, files, firewall, roles and features, Windows Update, storage and shares, network adapters, registry, scheduled tasks, certificates, devices, DNS and DHCP, performance counters, and a PowerShell console that needs a fresh password confirmation. Anything without its own page can be done with the cmdlet runner.

sections.title: Safety
sections.body: Every admin call is written to the Windows event log with the acting user. Destructive operations need a confirmation value checked by the server, not only by the browser.

features.title: App streaming
features.summary: Stream published Windows apps to any browser tab, or download a Remote Desktop file for a native window.
facts: Apache Guacamole 1.6.0 with encrypted JSON auth
Windows Server 2025 with Desktop Experience, never the DC

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Guests pick an app in the portal. For the browser, the portal builds a short-lived, signed and encrypted payload naming one RDP connection with the guest's own credentials and exchanges it for a Guacamole session. Guacamole stores no users, connections or passwords. For Windows, the portal hands out a `.rdp` file and only the app window appears.

sections.title: Licensing
sections.body: Guest sessions on an RD Session Host need RDS CALs (Per User) after a 120-day grace period. For a single kiosk-style use, a Windows 11 Pro or Enterprise PC can serve RemoteApps to one session at a time without CALs.

features.title: TempDesk Lite
features.summary: No Windows Server license: a Samba 4 domain controller in Docker on a Linux host with the same API.
facts: Same contract as the Windows agent

sections.title: What is the same
sections.body: Guest sign-ins, expiry and cleanup, Wi-Fi profiles, scripts, the allowlist, directory editing, Group Policy registry settings, Administrative Templates and security settings all work through the same API, so the portals do not care which backend they talk to.

sections.title: What differs
sections.body: The Samba agent reports its capabilities in `/health`. It has no Windows cmdlet runner, Group Policy preferences or WMI filters, and adds an allowlisted `samba-tool` runner instead. The portal hides any section whose capability is missing.

features.title: Answer File Studio
features.summary: Build and edit autounattend.xml in your browser: Guided templates for TempDesk, or Direct editing of every unattend setting with no template.
facts: Guided (TempDesk server, Guest PC, Custom templates) and Direct (the answer file itself)
The shared settings catalog, generator and rules engine, with quick fixes
Runs in your browser, nothing is uploaded

sections.title: Guided mode
sections.body: Templates open into the studio. **TempDesk server** builds Windows Server 2025 Core media with a static IP, the forest, the DSRM password and the portals choice, and downloads a kit with `autounattend.xml`, `TempDesk/firstboot.json` and the whole payload. **Guest PC** builds Windows 11 media that joins the domain in specialize with Microsoft-Windows-UnattendedJoin. **Custom** covers general Windows and Windows Server installs. Extra settings from the catalog, snippets and raw XML sit alongside the template.

sections.title: Direct mode
sections.body:
Direct mode has no template and no step-by-step forms: the answer file is the catalog model itself. The explorer shows the seven configuration passes; add any component the pass allows from a searchable picker, then edit every setting in a property editor generated from the catalog, with list editors for `wcm:action="add"` items, an Unset button that shows the default, and a link to the Microsoft reference page. XML is written only by the shared generator and read back by its parser, so the XML tab is fully two-way.

Open any existing `autounattend.xml` in Direct mode: every documented element maps to a control, and anything the reference does not describe is kept as an editable raw block, with a warning, in exactly the same place. Switch with **Guided | Direct** in the top bar. Guided to Direct keeps everything; Direct to Guided is offered only when a template can write the file exactly, and otherwise explains which parts would not fit. `?mode=direct` opens straight into Direct.

sections.title: Tools in both modes
sections.body: The setup flow canvas, disk layout and command timeline work on the same file. Problems come from the rules engine, with a quick fix where a safe one exists. The code editor (CodeMirror) offers autocomplete from the catalog, lint markers, folding and search. Compare against a saved version, a history entry or another file, simulate the setup pass by pass, and undo anything, including a mode switch.

features.title: Deployer app
features.summary: A Windows app that builds the install media, watches the unattended setup over the network and finishes the job.
facts: Windows Server 2025 Core or TempDesk Lite over SSH
Keeps real Git history of your answer files

sections.title: From blank VM to ready
sections.body: Windows Setup runs `FirstLogon.ps1` once from the install media: it copies the TempDesk folder to `C:\TempDesk`, applies the static IP, turns on PowerShell remoting, registers the `TempDesk Setup` startup task and creates the forest. After each reboot `Continue-Setup.ps1` waits for Active Directory, creates the OUs, groups and policies, installs the agent and, if chosen, the native portals, then removes the passwords from `firstboot.json` and reports READY.

sections.title: Download
sections.body: The installer is published on the GitHub releases page. It is not code signed yet, so check the SHA-256 published with the release.

features.title: Personal wording
features.summary: Upload a small JSON file with your own words for interface text. It changes labels and headings only.
facts: Up to 256 KiB, nesting up to 8 levels
Interface copy only, never generated files or data

sections.title: Rules
sections.body: Each entry maps a phrase (1 to 160 characters) to a replacement (up to 1000 characters). Duplicate keys, reserved names (`__proto__`, `prototype`, `constructor`) and control characters are rejected, and the whole file is validated before anything changes. Matching is whole-word, longest phrase first, and keeps the capitalization of the original.

sections.title: Where it lives
sections.body: On this website the file stays in your browser (localStorage). In the admin console it is stored on the server for that installation. It is never applied to generated XML, scripts, user names or other data, and it is never logged.

features.title: Language modes
features.summary: English, Cantonese (Traditional Chinese, Hong Kong) or both at once, everywhere.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Every interface string lives in two catalogs, `en.json` and `zh-HK.json`, with identical keys, checked by the tests. Bilingual mode shows the English text with the Cantonese line beneath it, which helps mixed groups at a shared desk. The choice is remembered in your browser.
